examples.explanation: The selected side chain is the one whose conjunctive name expresses the greater number of principal characteristic groups.
The senior ring system is selected according to the ring and ring-system seniority order.
A double bond linking the acyclic component to the ring system excludes conjunctive nomenclature.
A heteroatom in the side chain requires normal substitutive nomenclature.
The side-chain characteristic-group arrangement falls under the stated limitation.
Higher-priority characteristic groups directly attached to the cyclic component exclude conjunctive nomenclature.
Two characteristic groups of the principal kind on the ring require normal substitutive nomenclature.
The first analysis table constructs the conjunctive parent, prefix components, and resulting conjunctive and substitutive names.
The second analysis table constructs the benzeneheptanal parent and the formyl prefix before the final names.

value.value: Do not use conjunctive nomenclature when a double bond links the acyclic component to the ring system; when a double bond or heteroatom is present in the side chain; when two identical characteristic groups are located on the side chain without violating the maximum-number condition; when higher-priority characteristic groups are directly attached to the cyclic component; or when two or more characteristic groups of the principal kind are located on the ring or ring system. Use normal substitutive nomenclature in these cases.
Note: The PIN is the substitutive name.
